turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Hi — sure, happy to be here. Not much to prepare on my end, honestly.
What time did you go to bed last night?
"Around eleven, same as usual. I'm not one of those people who watches the clock about it — I just get sleepy and go."
Thanks. Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night, and would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

"Around six hours, I'd guess — went down at eleven, was up by five to. I'd call it decent, not great. The dog next door had me up around three for a while, but I got back off eventually and didn't feel too worse for wear this morning."
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed, and why did you choose to do that activity?
"Oh, just a crossword actually — I keep a book of them by the armchair. It settles my head down better than telly does, so that's usually the last thing before I turn the lights off."
That sounds like a nice routine. Over the past two weeks, what factors have most affected your sleep quality?

"Honestly, not much has changed — that neighbor's dog is a repeat offender, maybe two or three times this fortnight. Otherwise the work weeks throw me off more than anything, if I've got an early site visit I sometimes go to bed a bit keyed up thinking about the next day, but that's about the size of it."
Is that pretty typical for you, or has something about your sleep or routine changed recently?

"Pretty typical, yeah. If you'd asked me a year ago when I still had a proper schedule, I'd probably have said differently — but now that the workweek's a bit of a moving target, this is just what it looks like most of the time."
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

"Yeah, I'd say so. It's not perfect — you're never going to talk me into loving that dog — but I get enough decent nights that I'm not fussed about it. I stopped expecting flawless sleep a long time ago."
Thanks for sharing that. You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

"Honestly, no — I'd love it, but with the way work's gone lately, some weeks it just doesn't happen. I'm not going to lose sleep over losing sleep, if that makes sense — six hours that's decent quality suits me better than chasing a number."
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

"Honestly, it comes down to whether I know what the next day looks like. If it's an open week, I sleep like a rock. If I've got an early site visit or something's unresolved with a client, that's when I get the odd restless night — like last night, really."
Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

"Not really, no — by the time I'm winding down I've usually had enough screens for one day. I'll maybe glance at my phone once to check nothing's blown up with a client, then it goes on the charger in the other room."
Do you regularly use social media? If so, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
"Not really, no — I check in on Facebook now and then to see what my son's posted, but it's more of a daytime thing. By the evening I'm honestly not that fussed about scrolling."
Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps?
"No, not really — I've had a poke around with one out of curiosity when my son was going on about it, but it's not something I use day to day. Not really my world, that stuff."
Thanks, that makes sense. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

"Honestly? Getting up earlier — waking at 6:30 without an alarm is fine, but I'd like a bit more say over the schedule myself rather than it just happening to me. Other than that, I'm not fussed, six-ish decent hours does the job."

Thanks for explaining that. Now, just a few final background questions. (Feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.)

Could you tell me your age?
"Fifty-eight."
Thank you. And what is your profession?
"Quantity surveyor — semi-retired now, though I still do a bit of consulting for a couple of building firms."
Thanks. And what is your country of birth?
